The general crop protection (CP) market environment
During the first nine months of 2026, crop protection market volumes saw weaker than anticipated growth due to elevated farmer costs and just-in-time purchasing patterns, despite low channel inventories supporting healthy underlying crop protection demand. Additionally, crop protection pricing, particularly in the off-patent market, continued to remain under pressure, mainly due to lower farmer profitability, as well as persistently low active ingredient prices resulting from structural production overcapacity in China.
Overall market conditions varied across regions and crops, while farmer margins remained under pressure in many markets due to higher borrowing costs as well as higher fertilizer and fuel costs.
Geopolitical tensions and weather-related disruption continued to create uncertainty along the entire value chain from crop production, input costs and grower profitability. [1]
The Company is focused on turning stabilization into profitable growth and sustained value creation. Its strategy prioritizes selective growth in markets, segments and offerings where ADAMA can create clear value for customers and generate attractive returns. Execution is focused on four sources of value: (i) driving portfolio differentiation that meets grower needs; (ii) enhancing commercial capabilities to support profitable growth; (iii) shifting to a more competitive, flexible and asset-light supply and manufacturing network; and (iv) improving organizational design, processes, and systems to support better decisions and create additional value across the business. Across these areas, ADAMA remains focused on improving margins, generating cash, maintaining cost control and directing investment toward the highest-return opportunities.
During Q3 2026 ADAMA continued to register and launch multiple new products in markets across the globe, adding on to its differentiated product portfolio. ADAMA is a global company with manufacturing and formulation facilities in several locations around the world, principally in Israel, China and Brazil. It is headquartered and has three manufacturing sites in Israel. Despite regional tensions that have escalated on February 28, 2026, the Company's Israeli production sites and supply chain, including ports, continued to operate without significant delays allowing the Company to support its markets, and ongoing activities.
During March and early April 2026, the Company's Neot Hovav site suffered limited and localized damage caused by falling debris following missile interceptions in the southern region of Israel. No bodily injuries were reported, and an immediate safety-driven closure of the facilities was carried out, followed by a phased shutdown, also for safety reasons. The Company initiated comprehensive damage assessments. The direct damage to its core production facilities was not meaningful and was primarily limited to a finished goods warehouse, certain ancillary equipment and systems and an open storage area. Thereafter, the Company undertook certain restoration activities, and as of the date of this release Neot Hovav site has returned to normal operational status. The Company expects the overall impact of these occurrences to be non-material, also due to appropriate compensation from governmental authorities.
Additionally, in respect to changes in global tariff policies, despite the uncertainty regarding changes to trade and tariff policies around the world, the Company currently expects that the impact on its operations and business results will continue to be immaterial.
Revenues in the third quarter decreased by approximately 4% (-9% in RMB; -6% in CER) to $897 million compared to last year, reflecting a decline of 4% in volumes and 2% in prices, partially compensated by positive impact of foreign exchange rates.
The lower volumes resulted from lower market demand in certain regions due to higher farmer costs and weather conditions, partially compensated by new product introductions. Lower prices reflected the overall lower market pricing and weaker farmer purchasing power.
These results brought the revenues in the first nine months of 2026 to $2,997 million, 1% lower than last year (-5% in RMB terms; -4% in CER terms), reflecting a decrease of 3% in prices and 1% in volumes, partially moderated positive impact of foreign exchange rates.
Excluding the Company's decision in Q3 2025 to reduce the manufacture and sale of certain basic chemicals, sales would have increased in the first nine months period by 1% in comparison to the corresponding period in 2025. Third quarter sales are on a comparable basis.
In EAME, sales declined in the third quarter reflecting significantly weaker market consumption and lower crop-protection applications across several European markets due to weather impacts creating channel inventory build-up and due to elevated farmer input costs. Market-share gains partly mitigated the decline, while competitive and pricing pressure remained high, concentrated in specific off-patent active ingredients.
North America sales increased supported by growth across Professional Solutions, Consumer and Canada. US Ag was impacted by lower market prices mainly in commodity categories, while continuing to present growth in key products and customer segments. Pricing pressure and elevated inventories affected several US agricultural products.
Latin America: In Brazil, sales declined despite intensified commercial execution ahead of the soybean season particularly across fungicides and insecticides. This was offset by continued pricing pressure, farmer liquidity constraints and intense competition, particularly in commodity products.
In the rest of LATAM, sales increased supported by higher volumes, particularly in Argentina, following disciplined implementation of its strategic growth priorities across the region, despite continued competitive and pricing pressure and El-NiÃ±o impact in certain countries.
Asia-Pacific (APAC) excluding China: Sales increased supported by growth in Pacific and India more than offsetting a decline in other South-East Asia sales. Pacific benefited from fungicide demand in Southern and Western Australia supported by new product introductions. South-East Asia sales were impacted by El-NiÃ±o impact on demand.
In China , sales reflected the Company's decision to reduce manufacturing and sale of certain basic chemicals since Q3 2025 and low-margin products, leading to a decline in sales in the nine-month period while in the third quarter sales were on a comparable basis and increased, reflecting higher sales of brand formulations driven by new product launches and higher non-ag sales following better utilization rates.
Reported gross profit in the third quarter declined 14% to $204 million (gross margin of 22.7%) compared to $236 million (gross margin of 25.2%) last year. In the first nine months, reported gross profit declined 2% to $777 million (gross margin of 25.9%) compared to $792 million (gross margin of 26.2%) last year.
Adjustments to reported results : The adjusted gross profit includes mainly reclassification of inventory impairment, taxes and surcharge and excludes certain transportation costs (classified under operating expenses).
A djusted gross profit in the third quarter declined 11% to $228 million (gross margin of 25.4%) compared to $257 million (gross margin of 27.6%) last year. In the first nine months, adjusted gross profit declined 2% to $860 million (gross margin of 28.7%) compared to $878 million (gross margin of 29.0%) last year.
The decline in gross profit in the third quarter and first nine-month period was due to the decline in sales, as described above and negative cost impact. These impacts were slightly moderated by the improvement in the Company's sales mix of higher margin products and positive impact of exchange rates.
Reported operating expenses [3] in the third quarter were $214 million (23.8% of sales) compared to $205 million (22.0% of sales) last year. In the first nine months of 2026 reported operating expenses declined to $614 million (20.5% of sales) compared to $636 million (21.0% of sales) last year.
Adjustments to reported results : Please refer to the explanation regarding adjustments to the gross profit in respect to certain transportation costs, taxes and surcharges and inventory impairment.
The Company recorded certain non-operational items within its reported operating expenses amounting to an expense of $37 million in Q3 2026 and an income of $36 million in 9M 2026 in comparison to expenses of $26 million in Q3 2025 and $73 million in 9M 2025. These items in 2026 mainly include: (i) non-cash amortization charges in respect of transfer assets received from Syngenta related to the 2017 ChemChina-Syngenta acquisition; (ii) non-cash amortization net charges related to intangible assets created as part of the Purchase Price Allocation (PPA) on acquisitions; (iii) capital gain from sale of a subsidiary's logistics center in Israel; (iv) fixed asset impairment related to improvement of operational efficiency; and (v) restructuring costs. For further details on these non-operational items, please see the appendix to this release.
Adjusted operating expenses in the third quarter decreased to $197 million (21.9% of sales) compared to $201 million (21.5% of sales) last year. In the first nine months, adjusted operating expenses reached $653 million (21.8% of sales) compared to $641 million (21.2% of sales) last year.
In the third quarter operating expenses decreased despite the negative impact of exchange rates following tight expense discipline. In the nine-month period operating expenses were still higher reflecting the negative impact of exchange rates, an increase in employee compensation and an increase in H1 2026 in expenses supporting business growth, partially offset by capital gain from the disposal of fixed assets.
Reported operating income was a loss of $10 million (-1.2% of sales) in the third quarter compared to an income of $30 million (3.2% of sales) last year. In the first nine months, reported operating income increased 5% to $163 million (5.4% of sales) compared to $155 million (5.1% of sales) last year.
Adjusted operating income in the third quarter declined 45% to $31 million (operating margin of 3.4%) from $56 million (operating margin of 6.0%) last year. In the first nine months, adjusted operating income declined 12% to $207 million (operating margin of 6.9%) compared to $237 million (operating margin of 7.8%) last year.
The lower operating income in the third quarter reflected the lower gross profit, partially compensated by lower operating expenses. In the first nine months, the decline in operating income reflected lower gross profit and higher operating expenses.
Reported EBITDA in the third quarter declined by 16% to $87 million (EBITDA margin of 9.7%) from $104 million (EBITDA margin of 11.2%) last year. EBITDA reported in the first nine months increased 10% to $417 million (EBITDA margin of 13.9%) from $378 million (EBITDA margin of 12.5%) last year.
Adjusted EBITDA in the third quarter declined 22% to $93 million (EBITDA margin of 10.4%) from $120 million (EBITDA margin of 12.9%) last year. Adjusted EBITDA in the first nine months declined 8% to $395 million (EBITDA margin of 13.2%) from $430 million (EBITDA margin of 14.2%) last year.
Adjusted financial expenses decreased to $57 million in the third quarter compared to $68 million last year and in the first nine months decreased to $174 million compared to $204 million last year.
The lower financial expenses in the third quarter of 2026 reflected the positive impact of the CPI, improved overall loan terms, the benefit of the continued positive cash flow and lower hedging costs. In the first nine months of 2026 the lower financial expenses also reflected the better debt structure, following the buyback of bonds in Q2 2025.
Adjusted taxes on income amounted to an expense of $48 million in the third quarter compared to $8 million last year, and in the first nine months amounted to an expense of $44 million compared to $4 million last year. The Company recorded higher tax expense in the first nine months of 2026 comparing to 2025 mainly due to lower tax income compared to last year, recognized according to the accounting method of calculation of tax assets related to unrealized profits and due to lower tax income compared to last year from foreign exchange impact of the stronger BRL. In addition, during the third quarter of 2026 the company adjusted the tax asset in Brazil according to the projected statutory profit before tax.
Reported net loss reached $115 million in the third quarter compared to $48 million last year. Reported net loss in the first nine months reached $53 million compared to $59 million last year.
After reflecting the impact of the above-mentioned extraordinary and non-operational charges, adjusted net loss in the third quarter reached $74 million compared to $20 million last year. Adjusted net loss in the first nine months reached $11 million compared to an income of $29 million last year.
Trade working capital as of September 30, 2026, was $2,183 million compared to $2,093 million as of September 30, 2025. The increase in working capital was due to higher receivables which reflected lower sales with short collection terms, and a decrease in account payables and a slight decrease in inventory levels, both due to lower procurement compared to last year.
Cash Flow : Operating cash inflow of $94 million and $194 million was generated in the third quarter and first nine months period respectively, compared to an inflow of $89 million and $331 million in the respective periods in 2025. In the first nine months, lower operating cash inflow was mainly due to lower collections of basic chemicals and timing differences mainly in Q1 2025, partially offset by lower procurement in comparison to last year, in which the Company increased procurement and inventory in order to provide business continuity during the merging of entities in Israel.
Net cash used in investing activities was $35 million in the third quarter and $16 million in the first nine months, compared to $43 million and $131 million in the respective periods in 2025. The Company continued the execution of its strategy to prioritize the most critical investments in infrastructure, portfolio and innovation. Additionally, part of optimization of its existing asset base, the Company disposed fixed assets primarily in the first nine months, including a logistics center in Israel and old dismantled facilities in China. The higher cash used in investing activities in the first nine months last year also reflected the payment for earn out related to Agrinova, a controlled subsidiary of the Company.
Free cash inflow of $33 million was generated in the third quarter and $87 million in the first nine months compared to $22 million and $112 million in the respective periods in 2025, reflecting the aforementioned operating and investing cash flow dynamics.

ADAMA serves customers in dozens of countries globally, with direct presence in all top 20 markets. For more information, visit us at www.ADAMA.com .
